stories.title: Man released in Widdecombe murder investigation
stories.summary: A 26-year-old man arrested on suspicion of murdering former MP and MEP Ann Widdecombe has been released from custody and is no longer part of the investigation, British police said. Ms Widdecome, who was 78, was found dead at her home in Haytor on Dartmoor on Thursday after sustaining serious injuries. Devon and Cornwall Police confirmed the man's release from custody this morning, following his arrest yesterday. Assistant Chief Constable Matt Longman said: "Our priority remains identifying those responsible and ensuring that all available evidence is thoroughly examined.

stories.title: Renewed appeal over murder of Antoinette Smith
stories.summary: Gardaí are renewing their appeal for information in relation to the investigation into the murder of 27-year-old Antoinette Smith, whose remains were discovered on Glendoo Mountain, near the Lemass monument and close to Glencree/Enniskerry in Co Wicklow on 3 April 1988. On Saturday, 11 July 1987, Antoinette and a friend attended the David Bowie concert in Slane, Co Meath. They returned to Dublin by bus, arriving in Parnell Square at around 11pm. While in the club, they met two men that they knew. They joined the men's company and remained with them until they all left shortly after 2am.

stories.title: FSAI recalls some Capri-Suns over incorrect sugar label
stories.summary: The Food Safety Authority of Ireland has issued a recall notice for three batches of Capri-Sun Orange over the incorrect labelling of sugar content. The error, it said, may mislead consumers who need to monitor their sugar intake, including those with diabetes. The FSAI said some Capri-Sun Orange Zero multipacks actually contain drinks with the normal sugar level. It said this was due to a "packaging error" in which some Capri-Sun Orange multipacks contain pouches incorrectly labelled as the zero sugar product.

stories.title: Donald Trump hasn't forgotten about Greenland
stories.summary: Greenland’s capital city, Nuuk, gets very little light in January - a few pale hours between too long darknesses. It was in that thin, fading light, on one of the city’s main streets, that I stopped people and asked them about Donald Trump. "I don't like to talk about him because he spoils my sleep," a retired university lecturer told me. "I don't sleep very well because I'm afraid." "It was a nightmare - that he was coming with a ship. It was awful, that dream. I'm scared for his plans. We are scared. We are all scared," she said.

stories.title: Dermot Kennedy: From busker to Aviva history-maker
stories.summary: On Saturday night, Dermot Kennedy will walk onto the stage at the Aviva Stadium in front of more than 50,000 fans. Twenty-four hours later, he'll do it all again, becoming the first solo artist to perform two consecutive concerts at the Dublin venue. It's the latest landmark in a remarkable journey that has taken him from busking on Grafton Street to becoming one of Ireland's biggest musical success stories Every success story has a starting point, and for Dermot Kennedy it was the streets of Dublin. Long before he was selling out arenas and stadiums, the Rathcoole native was busking on Grafton Street, honing the powerful vocals and emotive songwriting that would later become his trademark. Performing for passers-by taught him how to capture an audience in an instant, while his years studying music at Maynooth University gave him the foundation to refine his craft as a songwriter and performer. His connection with Maynooth continued long after graduation in 2012. The Maynooth University Chamber Choir, a group he had admired during his student years, later collaborated with him on his music, bringing their voices to his album The Weight of the Woods, reflecting a full-circle moment.

stories.title: Appeal to conserve water amid risk to supplies
stories.summary: People are being urged to conserve water as the heatwave continues. Uisce Eireann said water is being consumed more quicky that it can be produced and replenished in local reservoirs. A Status Yellow high temperature warning for 13 counties will be in place until tomorrow morning. The warning covers Carlow, Kildare, Kilkenny, Laois, Longford, Meath, Offaly, Westmeath, Wexford, Cork, Limerick, Tipperary and Waterford, with temperatures expected to reach as high as 30C in places.
